title: Bond investors starting to doubt long-term prospects of some AI hyperscalers: BondCliQ's Chris White
key_facts: Chris White, CEO of BondCliQ and ViableMkts, spoke to CNBC on 14 Oct 2026.
He says bond investors have started to doubt the long-term prospects of many AI hyperscalers, citing CoreWeave and Oracle.
Their debt is about 5% of a $258 billion total he cited, but its short maturity is the bigger worry.
Oracle raised $25 billion in bonds in February; CoreWeave raised $3.7 billion in convertible notes in September.
They must refinance in five to seven years and may need to offer a yield premium.
Microsoft is the only triple-A-rated AI hyperscaler and would set the benchmark if it issued bonds.
Yields on 10-year and 30-year US Treasuries were above 5%.
quote_evidence: "They're going to have to refinance this debt in the next five to seven years. And that then makes them a lot more sensitive to, I would say, the shorter-term interest rate conditions," White said.
The fixed-income expert also noted that as bond oversupply begins, it would also affect the U.S. government's ability to raise capital.
why_it_matters_hint: Bond markets, which react over weeks, are starting to price in AI doubt.
